newsitem.title: LEBANON: Red Army fighters in Lebanon threaten suicide.
newsitem.headline: Red Army fighters in Lebanon threaten suicide.

text.p: Five Red Army guerrillas arrested in Beirut will commit suicide if Lebanon decides to hand them over to Japan, a guerrilla told the Monday issue of a Beirut newspaper.

"If the Lebanese government decides to do that (hand us over) we will commit suicide inside the jail to protect our comrades," Masao Adachi, 57, said at the Roumyeh jail in mountains northeast of Beirut.

He was speaking to al-Kifah al-Arabi which appeared for the first time on newstands on Monday. It was the first time the press interviewed any of the guerrillas since they were arrested on February 15.
Lebanese judicial authorities charged the five Japanese Red Army guerrillas 10 days ago with passport forgery and other offences carrying up to 10 years in jail.
Lebanon said the suspects would be tried in Lebanon for offences committed in the country, eliminating the possiblity of a quick extradition Japan had hoped for.
Lebanon and Japan do not have an extradition agreement.
Asked where other Red Army guerrillas were, Adachi told the newspaper's editor-in-chief Walid al-Husseini: "If I tell you now, why commit suicide later on?".

Asked whether they pleaded guilty when interrogated, Adachi said: "That is true. We have confessed to the investigative judge. What can we do? We cannot have Japanese passports. Is there another alternative"?
He said all five guerrillas were arrested in an apartment in Beirut.

Adachi was speaking on behalf of the four other detainees, three of whom were present during the interview. They were Kazua Tohira, Haruo Wako, and Kozo Okamoto -- involved in the May 1972 shootout at Tel Aviv's Lod airport in which 24 people died and 100 were injured.
Okamoto was captured by Israeli forces and sentenced to life imprisonment but was released in a Palestinian-Israeli prisoner swap in May, 1985.
The fifth guerrilla, Mariko Yamamoto, was held in a women's jail in Beirut.

Asked what they expected from Arabs after their arrest, Adachi said: "I don't believe the Arab states and the Arab people can abandon us so easily. We have fought on their side when they were fighting Israel. And we will fight if they fight again".
